base_properties.human_readable: QWERTY Keyboard Layout as Natural Standard

stakeholders.name: keyboard_manufacturers
stakeholders.situation: Produce keyboards with QWERTY layout as the overwhelming default. Retooling for alternative layouts would require capital investment and market education; maintaining QWERTY means zero switching cost and compatibility with the installed base of typists and software.

stakeholders.name: typing_instruction_industry
stakeholders.situation: Built curricula, certification programs, and instructional materials around QWERTY. Switching to an alternative layout would obsolete existing materials and require retraining instructors; QWERTY persistence means their capital remains productive.

stakeholders.name: incumbent_software_platforms
stakeholders.situation: Ship operating systems and applications with QWERTY as the default input mapping. Supporting alternative layouts is technically trivial but adds configuration surface area; QWERTY universality means one mapping serves effectively all users.

stakeholders.name: proficient_qwerty_typists
stakeholders.situation: Have invested years building muscle memory on QWERTY. Switching to a more efficient layout would require months of retraining at reduced productivity; QWERTY persistence protects that sunk investment. They also bear the opportunity cost of not having learned a faster layout initially.

stakeholders.name: new_typists
stakeholders.situation: Learn QWERTY because it is the only layout with universal hardware and software support, widespread instruction, and social expectation. They bear the cost of learning a suboptimal layout but have no practical alternative given the installed base.

stakeholders.name: alternative_layout_advocates
stakeholders.situation: Promote Dvorak, Colemak, or other layouts as ergonomically and speed-superior. They produce evidence of efficiency gains but cannot overcome the coordination problem: no individual gains from switching unless others do, and manufacturers have no incentive to lead.

stakeholders.name: ergonomics_researchers
stakeholders.situation: Study typing efficiency, repetitive strain injury rates, and layout optimization. They document QWERTY's suboptimality but observe that the coordination lock-in makes their findings practically inert.

six_questions.coordination_function: Provides a universal input standard: every keyboard, every typist, every software application expects the same key arrangement, eliminating configuration overhead and enabling instant interoperability.
six_questions.transfer_function: Moves the opportunity cost of suboptimal layout efficiency from manufacturers and the instruction industry (who would bear switching costs) to new typists (who learn the slower layout) and proficient typists (who carry the sunk cost of their training).
six_questions.absent_voices: Alternative layout advocates and ergonomics researchers document the efficiency loss but are structurally excluded from the decision: manufacturers face no competitive pressure to switch, and individual typists face prohibitive retraining costs.
six_questions.disappearance_rationale: If QWERTY disappeared overnight and all keyboards/software reset to layout-agnostic, the market would reorganize around competing layouts, typing instruction would fragment across standards, and early movers would face coordination risk until a new equilibrium formed.
six_questions.founding_problem: Early typewriters jammed when adjacent keys were struck in rapid succession; QWERTY separated common letter pairs to reduce mechanical interference.
six_questions.founding_problem_corroboration: The mechanical jamming problem was solved by the 1930s with improved typewriter mechanisms and disappeared entirely with electronic keyboards. Ergonomics researchers, historians of technology, and alternative layout advocates all attest the founding problem is obsolete; only the layout persists.

commentary.narrative_context: QWERTY was designed in the 1870s to prevent mechanical typewriter jams by separating frequently-paired keys. The mechanical constraint disappeared by the 1930s, yet QWERTY persists as the global standard 140 years later. The constraint is CLAIMED as mountain (a natural coordination equilibrium that would re-emerge even if alternatives were tried) while the metrics describe modest extraction accumulating over time as the founding function became obsolete. Keyboard manufacturers, typing instruction providers, and software platforms benefit from QWERTY's persistence through avoided switching costs; new typists and proficient typists locked into muscle memory bear the opportunity cost of the suboptimal layout. The engine measures whether this is a genuine coordination equilibrium or a false summit where beneficiary presence indicates constructed persistence.
key_agents: keyboard_manufacturers: Primary beneficiary (organized/mobile) — avoid retooling costs by maintaining QWERTY
typing_instruction_industry: Primary beneficiary (organized/mobile) — curricula and materials remain productive
incumbent_software_platforms: Primary beneficiary (institutional/arbitrage) — one default mapping serves all users
proficient_qwerty_typists: Dual position (organized/identity_locked) — benefit from protecting sunk training investment, bear opportunity cost of suboptimal layout
new_typists: Primary target (powerless/trapped) — learn suboptimal layout with no practical alternative
alternative_layout_advocates: Excluded (moderate/constrained) — document efficiency gains but cannot overcome coordination lock-in
ergonomics_researchers: Analytical observer (moderate/analytical) — measure the efficiency loss
commentary.logic_rationale: Extraction is low but non-zero (0.18) because QWERTY imposes a measurable efficiency cost on all typists relative to optimized layouts, but the cost is diffuse and the coordination benefit is real. Suppression is low (0.22) because no party actively enforces QWERTY — it persists through network effects and switching costs, not coercion. Theater is very low (0.12) because the coordination function is genuine; the extractive component is the opportunity cost of the suboptimal layout, not performative maintenance. Accessibility collapse is high (0.78) because once QWERTY became universal, learning any other layout meant incompatibility with the installed base — alternatives collapsed not because they were inferior but because they were unsupported. Resistance is low (0.15) because alternative layout advocates exist but face a coordination problem, not a natural law. The measurement series shows modest extraction accumulation as the founding problem (mechanical jamming) became obsolete but the layout persisted.
commentary.directionality_logic: Manufacturers, instruction providers, and software platforms are structural beneficiaries: QWERTY persistence means zero switching cost for them, and they would bear the coordination risk of leading a transition. Their directionality is near the beneficiary end. Proficient typists are identity-locked: their muscle memory is fused with QWERTY, making retraining prohibitively costly; they benefit from QWERTY's persistence (protects sunk investment) but also bear its opportunity cost (learned a suboptimal layout). New typists are trapped targets: they learn QWERTY because it is the only universally supported option, bearing the full opportunity cost with no exit. Alternative layout advocates are excluded rather than coordinated.
commentary.perspectival_gap: From the beneficiary seats (manufacturers, instruction industry, platforms), QWERTY is a stable coordination equilibrium that no party has reason to disturb. From the trapped target seat (new typists), the same structure operates as a locked-in suboptimal standard they must accept to participate. From the analytical seat, the question is whether QWERTY would re-emerge if the slate were wiped clean, or whether its persistence depends on the beneficiaries' collective inaction. The engine computes this divergence from the structural data.
commentary.mandatrophy_analysis: The founding problem (mechanical jamming) is dead; QWERTY persists as a coordination standard. The mandatrophy question is whether this is genuine coordination (would re-emerge even without beneficiaries) or constructed persistence (beneficiaries' switching costs keep it locked in). The omega variables address this: if QWERTY would NOT re-emerge in a clean-slate scenario, its persistence is partly extractive. The modest extraction and low suppression suggest the coordination function is real but the efficiency cost is non-zero.

omegas.question: If all keyboards, software, and typists reset to layout-agnostic tomorrow, would QWERTY re-emerge as the equilibrium, or would a more efficient layout win?
omegas.resolution_mechanism: Natural experiment from a new input modality (e.g., VR typing, brain-computer interfaces) where no installed base exists: observe which layout early adopters converge on when switching costs are zero.
omegas.impact: If QWERTY would NOT re-emerge, its current persistence is path-dependent lock-in rather than natural coordination, and the measured extraction represents the efficiency cost of that lock-in. If it WOULD re-emerge, the extraction is the inherent cost of any universal standard.
omegas.description: Whether QWERTY is a natural equilibrium or path-dependent artifact.

omegas.question: Does QWERTY persist because it is the natural coordination point, or because the parties who would bear switching costs (manufacturers, instruction industry) have no incentive to lead a transition?
omegas.resolution_mechanism: Counterfactual analysis: if a dominant manufacturer or platform unilaterally switched to an optimized layout and absorbed the transition cost, would the market follow, or would QWERTY's coordination advantage keep it dominant?
omegas.impact: If beneficiary inaction is necessary for QWERTY's persistence, the constraint is a false summit — it looks natural but depends on identifiable parties' structural position. If QWERTY would persist even with active beneficiary support for alternatives, it is a genuine mountain.
omegas.description: Whether beneficiary presence is incidental or constitutive of QWERTY's persistence.

omegas.question: What is the actual efficiency loss from QWERTY relative to optimized layouts, measured in typing speed, error rate, and repetitive strain injury incidence?
omegas.resolution_mechanism: Meta-analysis of controlled studies comparing QWERTY to Dvorak, Colemak, and other layouts across diverse typing tasks and user populations.
omegas.impact: A large efficiency gap would support higher extractiveness and suggest QWERTY's persistence imposes substantial opportunity cost; a small gap would support the mountain framing where the coordination benefit dominates.
omegas.description: Magnitude of the efficiency cost QWERTY imposes.

network.dual_formulation_note: This story is one reading of the QWERTY kernel. A sibling reading would claim QWERTY is pure coordination (no beneficiaries, alternatives lapsed naturally) and would omit the beneficiary declarations. The two readings produce different ε values and different FSM verdicts; they are linked as a constraint family but are structurally distinct claims.
